haiku-low.q1: Fallback: 20 popular items with fallback=true and fallback_reason (feature_timeout or no_features), plus the active version ID.
haiku-low.q2: Old bundles keep serving until 6 hours past materialized_at, then requests fall back to popular items (stale_features). Two failed runs' fallback rule conflicts; open.
haiku-low.q3: No; shadow output is never shown to users, and shadow runs off the request path, so shadow failures don't change the response.
haiku-low.q4: Users with fresh, complete features whose hash bucket is below shadow_percent (10%). Fallback users get no shadow.
haiku-low.q5: Eligible, at least 7 days in shadow, error rate under 0.5%, inference p99 under 80 ms, and recorded ML lead approval.
haiku-low.q6: Not decided; product has not chosen. The plan keeps both a live A/B step and direct 100% open (step 18, question 7).
haiku-low.q7: Instances poll the config every 15 seconds or watch it, load the named version if missing, and swap pointers in memory. No restart.
haiku-low.q8: It reuses the bundle read in step 2, copied into the queue event. Separate workers run it off the request path; queueing never blocks.
haiku-low.q9: Events are dropped and counted; the user's response is unchanged, and the logged sampling rate reads lower than configured.
haiku-low.q10: Candidate results and active items go to the append-only shadow results store (hashed user IDs); a daily job compares overlap, rank correlation, coverage and spread.
haiku-low.q11: Registration marks it ineligible when a required feature is missing from the catalog, and it cannot be set active or shadow.
haiku-low.q12: Config is set back to the previous version. It stays loaded on instances, so no download; polling or watch applies it within 1 minute.

sonnet.q1: Fallback: 20 popular items with fallback=true, fallback_reason (feature_timeout/feature_error or no_features) and the active version ID. The feature read limit is 30 ms.
sonnet.q2: It keeps using the old bundles already in the online store (a failed run leaves them in place) until each bundle's materialized_at is over 6 hours old. Then those are stale (stale_features) and requests fall back to popular items. Alert at 2 hours of lag. The doc has an unresolved conflict: a draft said two consecutive failures cause fallback, but the 6-hour rule decides (open question 6).
sonnet.q3: No. Shadow output is never shown to a user. A shadow failure has no effect on the response: the response goes out first, the queue add is non-blocking, and a full queue just drops the event and counts it. Shadow errors are only logged.
sonnet.q4: Only users whose request passed the feature step with fresh, complete features and whose bucket is under shadow_percent. Bucket = hash(shadow_salt + user_id) mod 100, with a stable hash such as SHA-256. Fallback users get no shadow. The shadow cohort is a fixed 10% of users who have features. The candidate must also be eligible and loaded, otherwise shadow_skipped is logged.
sonnet.q5: At least 7 qualifying days in shadow (days that met the minimum eligible-request count, with no gap that ended shadow). Candidate error rate under 0.5% and inference p99 under 80 ms over the shadow window. Version still eligible. ML lead approval recorded in the registry with identity and timestamp. The switch is complete only once confirmed across the fleet.
sonnet.q6: Undecided. Product has not decided. The plan keeps both options open through the allocation table (step 18) and chooses neither.
sonnet.q7: The control plane writes the serving config with compare-and-set on revision. Each instance is notified when the config record changes and also polls every 15 seconds as a backup. It loads any named version it lacks from the artifact store, warms it with a test inference, then swaps the in-memory pointers. There is no restart or redeploy. Instances report applied revision and active_version.
sonnet.q8: The worker runs the candidate on the feature bundle captured at request time (step 5), not a fresh read, so both models see the same inputs. It adds no latency because the response goes to the client first. The queue add is non-blocking, and separate workers with their own capacity, timeout and circuit breaker run it off the request path.
sonnet.q9: Events are dropped and counted when the queue is full or the worker pool is saturated, so the effective sampling rate reads lower than configured. The user's response is unchanged. If active p99 rises, cap or stop the shadow pool. The kill switch is shadow_percent set to 0.
sonnet.q10: Shadow results (candidate output with the active items) go to the shadow results store, an append-only log with hashed user IDs. A daily aggregation plus live dashboards compare them. Metrics are candidate error rate, inference p99, agreement with active (overlap at 20 and rank correlation), catalog coverage, spread across users, and eligible request counts. Active path p99 and error rate are also checked before and after shadow. Where active predictions are recorded on their own is NOT STATED beyond the shadow event and results store.
sonnet.q11: At registration, the control plane compares the version's required-feature list with the feature catalog. A version with any missing feature is marked ineligible and cannot be set as shadow or active. A feature removed from materialization also makes any version that requires it ineligible. At request time, a second check on each required feature in the bundle falls back with missing_feature without calling the model.
sonnet.q12: The control plane sets the config back to the previous version with the same compare-and-set write as step 9. That version stays loaded in memory on each instance and in the registry, so no download is needed. It takes effect within 1 minute because of the config watch plus 15-second polling, and the control plane confirms the revision across the fleet. It needs no ML lead approval (recommended, to be confirmed). The last resort is serving mode popular_only.
